item.title: Fantasy Football Week 11 wide receiver rankings
item.description: Fantasy football Week 11 wide receiver rankings are here, helping managers navigate the matchups and identify the best options at one of the most important positions in their lineups. With target volume, consistency, big-play ability, and touchdown potential all factoring into weekly value, these rankings break down which wide receivers should be prioritized heading into this week’s NFL action. MORE: Fantasy Football studs & duds Week 10 of 2026 NFL season Ranks 10-8 Oct 18, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Tennessee Titans wide receiver Carnell Tate (14) reacts after scoring a touchdown during the second half against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images 10. Carnell Tate-Titans: Why not have a Titan on this list…if there was ever a week to have one, it’s this week, with the Titans heading to Big D to play the Cowboys and their atrocious pass defense. The Cowboys have given up the second-most points in the NFC, and even though the Titans have only won one game this year, they scored 59 points in their last two matchups. Tate has been out with a shoulder injury but is expected back this week. 9. Malik Nabers-Giants: Nabers is just outside the top 10 in receiving yds and tied for seventh in catches. His only drawback this year has been his red-zone work and inability to score, with only two TDs. The Giants are only scoring 22.5pts per game, and ultimately, their lack of scoring output will be their demise. But that said, Nabers is their clear No. 1 receiving option, regardless of who is getting him the ball. Coming off a home loss, the Giants can’t afford a losing streak, especially with both losses coming at home. They’ll need to put out maximum effort against this tough matchup against the Jaguars. John Harbaugh normally has his teams prepared for situations like this. Expect Nabers to be all over this offensive game plan. 8. Parker Washington-Jaguars: While Washington lacks the receptions of other WR1 receivers in the league, he makes up for it in overall production. While he only has 36 catches, which is outside the top 20, he is 15th in fantasy pts among WRs, and 15th in receiving yds…and he averages nearly 18yds per catch. But, most importantly, he’s tied for sixth in TD receptions with six. Ranks 7-4 Oct 11, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III (10) warms up before the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images 7. Luther Burden-Bears: Burden has supplanted Rome Odunze as the team’s WR1, and the QB/WR connection with Caleb Williams will be a problem for defenses for the next decade. In only his second season, he’s on pace to finish the season with a stat line of 90 catches, 1,200 yards, and eight TDs…nearly doubling last year’s output. He faces a Saints team this week that has given up over 26pts per game. And at home, look for the Bears to put up over 30pts, with Burden heavily involved. 6. J

item.title: Parsons’ return imminent but doesn’t solve Packers’ biggest problem
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Micah Parsons #1 of the Green Bay Packers looks on prior to the game against the Carolina Panthers of the game at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images For all of the Green Bay Packers’ issues through ten games of the 2026 season, getting to the quarterback generally hasn’t been one of them. The Packers’ defense ranks fourth in the NFL in sacks this year, with pressure helping the team rank second in interceptions and fifth in overall passer rating against. Now the cavalry appears set to arrive. Micah Parsons is on his way back, seemingly with the intent of playing next Wednesday against the Los Angeles Rams, and his presence will only further bolster the team’s ability to get after the quarterback. It remains to be seen how he will be deployed — expect a light workload for the next few games, perhaps with him only playing on passing downs — but his return should provide an emotional lift as well as a physical one for a defense that’s already playing well. As that last phrase suggests, though, the defense isn’t really the Packers’ problem right now. That is of course the offensive line, where some recent front office decisions have helped set the table for a catastrophic season up front. One can’t help wondering if this team would be functioning better had Elgton Jenkins been kept around for one more year; had the team not invested so much money in Aaron Banks; had Anthony Belton — wait, the front office drafted him as a guard and he’s been thrust in at tackle by circumstance and the coaching staff, so that one probably isn’t on the front office. And then there is that coaching staff. From a poor overall offensive game plan last week against Minnesota to players seemingly having no idea what they’re doing on a play-to-play basis, the offensive coaches should have spent their few off days in a shortened bye week doing some serious self-evaluation. So, while Parsons’ return is an exciting storyline for the Packers, it almost feels like we’re adding the whipped cream on top of an excellent pumpkin pie while smoke is billowing out of the oven as the turkey burns. So let’s get that main course under control, yeah? Packers cut Pierre Strong to clear roster spot for Micah Parsons’ imminent return | Packersnews.com ($) Strong’s release is all but assuredly a move to open a roster spot for #1, and we should probably expect Strong to return to the practice squad if he clears waivers. Grand Theft Contract: Six Worst Packers Free-Agent Signings of GTA Era | SI.com I’m amused by the conceit of this article, but it does illustrate just how bad two of the free agent contracts of the 2025 offseason were. When you get basically nothing out of a 4-year, $48 million deal (Nate Hobbs) and a 4-year, $77 million contract (Aaron Banks), it’s going to set you back significantly. Brian Gutekunst vindicated as former Packers struggle in new homes | Packers Wire Stil

item.title: ATP increases player compensation to $350m
item.description: The season-ending ATP Finals is currently taking place in Turin [Getty Images] The men's ATP Tour is promising its players rewards of at least $350m in 2028 - but the board has delayed a decision on hotly disputed changes to doubles until next month. The bonus pool will increase from the current $21.5m to $50m in 2028, with payments offered to players ranked in the world's top 30 at the start of each Masters 1000 event. The world number one will receive the highest bonus of $2m for each of the Masters events they play. A total of $25m will also be shared out between the world's top 250 players at the end of each season, with the goal for everyone to receive $100,000. That would make a significant difference to the finances of lower-ranked players. Players will also no longer be penalised so directly for missing tournaments through injury. World number two Jannik Sinner, for example, won five Masters events in a row between March and May, but may only qualify for 25% of his bonus as he has not been able to play since Wimbledon. Doubles changes 'a sensitive issue' Proposed changes to the doubles - which includes halving draw sizes and reducing the percentage of prize money from 20% to 10% - have received fierce opposition from the players. In October, more than 150 men's doubles players wrote an open letter to the ATP Tour urging them to reconsider "drastic" changes to the format. Chairman Andrea Gaudenzi told BBC Sport the governing body of men's tennis needed "a bit more time to reach consensus". "It is a sensitive issue," he said. "I hope we find the right balance between the players' and the tournaments' demands, and I truly hope we reach a compromise." The proposals will now be voted on next month. Doubles players have said the changes would make it "effectively impossible" for anyone outside the top 30 to make a living from the sport. There may be a hint of compromise in the air, but Gaudenzi still believes at least some of the doubles money needs to be redirected towards singles players. "It's impossible to make everyone happy. It's something we do not take lightly, but we also cannot ignore the fans and the broadcasters - [just] like any entertainment business," he said. "Whether you are a musician or an actor, it needs to be rewarded as a function of the entertainment you provide to the fans." Gaudenzi told Britain's Henry Patten, who was unhappy he and CEO Eno Polo were not present when Patten and Harri Heliovaara received the year-end number one trophy, that he had no intention of undermining their achievement. "I understand his disappointment and he's obviously also driven by what we are discussing, and I do understand it's quite emotional their side," Gaudenzi added. "But I was here in the hotel together with Eno - we were actually fighting and negotiating twelve hours a day to get this deal done - so we were really in the trenches all day long." 'Don't expect big changes' over 2028 off-season The ATP Board has also approved the format

item.title: 'I'll tell more' - Thomas Frank teases truth behind Tottenham sacking as he prepares for Crystal Palace rescue mission
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Newcastle United - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Thomas Frank has officially been unveiled as the new Crystal Palace manager, and the Dane wasted no time in addressing his complicated history with former employers Tottenham. As he prepares to lead the struggling Eagles out of the Premier League relegation zone, Frank suggested there is a deeper story behind his short-lived tenure in North London. Frank takes Palace reins after turbulent Spurs spell Crystal Palace appointed the 53-year-old Dane on Monday on a contract until June 2029, replacing Pierre Sage. Thursday afternoon's unveiling marked Frank's first managerial role since Tottenham sacked him earlier this year after under eight months in charge. Before his troubled north London stint, Frank established Brentford in the Premier League and earned a Manager of the Year nomination. Following his Spurs dismissal, he travelled across Japan, Australia, and Denmark before taking over the Eagles. Dane promises future clarity on Tottenham departure Expecting questions about his former club, Frank admitted: "I know today is a lot about me". While keeping the focus on Palace, he suggested the full story of his Spurs exit will eventually surface. "It’s something I’ve… maybe one day I’ll tell a little bit more about it," Frank said. "I understand why it’s also interesting. I think it’s more about Palace in general today. What can I say? I always said the day I got sacked, I’ll have time to travel, so I think I was relatively quick over it." He added: "But of course you want success, and I’m competitive, so I think that answer probably demands a little bit more time, which I am happy to do one day." Infamous Arsenal cup gaffe still baffles new Eagles boss Frank's Spurs spell unravelled in January when he was pictured drinking from an Arsenal coffee cup ahead of a 3-2 defeat to Bournemouth. For fans already disillusioned with his style of play, the blunder was the final straw, and a five-match winless league run sealed his sacking a month later. Asked if he might accidentally use a cup belonging to Palace's fierce rivals Brighton, Frank smiled. "I hope not," he replied, adding: "I still think it’s a fantastic story." He remains baffled by the backlash to the honest mistake: "I know, and I still don’t understand, how anyone can think that I will drink from a cup from an opponent’s team, that their supporters don’t like, on purpose. Come on. But what a story, huh, to discuss?" Relegation battle and Europa League test await Frank faces an immediate test in lifting Crystal Palace off the bottom of the Premier League table, starting with Saturday's trip to Coventry. Arresting their domestic slump quickly is vital to sparking a survival push. He must also balance European duties, with Palace hosting Real Sociedad in the Europa League next Thursday. Managing energy levels across both fronts will be crucial as the Dane bids to restore his Premier League credentials.

item.title: Week 11 fantasy football trade targets: Rice, Swift, Cousins, Pitts for playoff runs
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice is the strongest Week 11 fantasy football trade target because his steady catch totals line up with a playoff schedule in which all three opponents rank top 11 in points allowed to receivers. Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins , Chicago Bears running back D’Andre Swift and Atlanta Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. round out the list, and each faces at least two favorable matchups during the Weeks 15-17 fantasy playoffs. MORE: Week 11 fantasy football PPR rankings: Burrow tops QBs as Bowers injury looms Kirk Cousins, QB, Minnesota Vikings Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) looks to throw in the first quarter against the Green Bay Packers | Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Last week: 21-of-31, 207 yds, 2 TD, 1 INT, 30-10 W at Packers This week: at 49ers (Mexico City), Sun., Nov. 22, 8:20 p.m. ET Minnesota sent Las Vegas a 2027 third-round pick to bring Cousins back at the deadline . He’d thrown 20 touchdown passes in nine starts for the Raiders. His Vikings debut was steady rather than flashy, but he leaned on Justin Jefferson with 13 targets, and Jefferson turned them into a season-high nine catches. Cousins’ 207 yards in Green Bay won’t jump off the page. What matters more is that he gets the ball to Jefferson on time, and the Vikings have their most functional offense in weeks. ROS FF Strength of Schedule: Minnesota opens the fantasy playoffs at home against Detroit, which allows the most fantasy points to quarterbacks. The Vikings then host Washington (sixth-most) and visit the Jets (11th-most), so Cousins has three top-11 matchups. MORE: Week 11 fantasy football QB start-sit: Goff, Nix, Purdy, Ward D’Andre Swift, RB, Chicago Bears Chicago Bears running back D’Andre Swift (4) leaves the field after defeating the Seattle Seahawks | Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Last game: 12 car., 31 yds; 0 rec., 27-24 W vs. Buccaneers This week: vs. Saints, Sun., Nov. 22, 1 p.m. ET Swift’s 31-yard game against Tampa Bay, Chicago’s bye and Kyle Monangai’s return to full practice have raised questions about Swift’s workload. Monangai handled 30 carries in Week 4 after Swift lost a fumble, but the second-year back said his turf toe hasn’t fully healed: “The time off definitely helped… but it’s going to be there .” Swift has run for 576 yards and scored 10 touchdowns this season, so the lead job should still be his. His Week 11 game against New Orleans, which allows the most fantasy points to running backs, starts a stretch of mostly favorable matchups. ROS FF Strength of Schedule: Chicago visits Miami (sixth-most to running backs) in Week 14 and Buffalo (10th) in Week 15, then hosts Green Bay (seventh) in Week 16. Detroit in Week 17 is the drawback, since the Lions allow the third-fewest. item.title: Colts to consider quarterback change after blowout loss to Texans
item.description: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards and an interception in a loss to the Houston Texans on Thursday in Houston. File Photo by Joe Marino/UPI Nov. 20 (UPI) -- The Indianapolis Colts will "evaluate everything," including a quarterback change, coach Shane Steichen said after a loss to the Houston Texans. Colts starter Daniel Jones completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards and an interception in the 26-3 setback Thursday in Houston. The veteran quarterback posted a passer rating of 43.9 over his last two games -- the worst two-game stretch of his career. "We'll evaluate everything," Steichen told reporters, when asked if Jones was still his starting quarterback. Jones completed a career-low 58.4% of his throws for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns and a league-high 13 interceptions through 11 starts this season. The eight-year veteran also lost three fumbles for the 3-8 Colts. Indianapolis Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson went 0 for 2 on pass attempts in the fourth quarter of a loss to the Houston Texans on Thursday in Houston. File Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI SAFETY. WILL ANDERSON JR. IS A MONSTER. Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones completed a career-low 58.4% of his throws through his first 11 starts of 2026. File Photo by Archie Carpenter/UPI INDvsHOU on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus https://t.co/E7sYceCOiZ— NFL (@NFL) November 20, 2026 Coach Shane Steichen said Indianapolis Colts will "evaluate everything" after a lopsided loss to the Houston Texans on Thursday in Houston. File Photo by Archie Carpenter/UPI On Thursday, Jones helped the Colts drive for a field goal on the game's opening possession. He failed to complete 10 of his next 15 passes as the Texans scored 23 unanswered points. Steichen opted to replace Jones with backup Anthony Richardson for the Colts' final drive in the fourth quarter. The Indianapolis Colts signed quarterback Daniel Jones (17) to a two-year, $88 million contract in March. File Photo by Craig Lassig/UPI "I thought he could do some things better," Steichen said of Jones. "Obviously, there was a good pass rush coming at him, for sure. But we'll go back and evaluate the tape." Richardson, who requested a trade last off-season, went 0 for 2 in relief of Jones. He also saw action in the fourth quarter of the Colts' Week 10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. He went 2 for 2 for 8 yards in that appearances. Jones signed a two-year, $88 million contract with the Colts in March. He has a salary cap hit of $46.8 million next season, with a scheduled void year in 2028. "I understand where we are as a team," Jones said. "I understand it's an issue to score three points. We've gotta be better offensively. I'm the quarterback, so I'm responsible. I've gotta play better. I know that. That's the job." Richardson, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, is on the final year of his rookie contract. item.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo downplays Bucks reunion after leading Heat to huge win
item.description: Giannis Antetokounmpo made his first meeting with the Milwaukee Bucks since joining the Miami Heat count, scoring a game-high 27 points on 7-for-11 shooting to lead Miami to a 137-130 victory on Wednesday. The Greek Freak stayed focused on helping his new team rather than showing emotion toward his former franchise. Tyler Herro also faced his old team after spending his entire NBA career in Miami before the blockbuster trade sent him to Milwaukee. Giannis said it wasn’t weird to face the Bucks for the first time since the trade and he didn’t prepare differently mentally or physically. #Heat pic.twitter.com/uiBce8cEs8 — Zachary Weinberger (@ZachWeinberger) November 19, 2026 Antetokounmpo showed little interest in making his return to face Milwaukee a major event. Having played 13 years for the Bucks, the Miami forward approached Wednesday’s matchup like any other regular-season contest and carried that attitude into his postgame media session. “I don’t think it was weird,” commented the Bucks star. “It wasn’t weird. Basketball is basketball. I tried to go out there, tried to do whatever I could to help my team win.” Giannis Antetokounmpo’s new focus wit the Miami Heat Nov 18, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo (7) dunks against the Bucks during the third quarter at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Giannis remains focused on contributing to Miami’s success, regardless of who stands on the opposite side of the court, including his former team, the Bucks. “I think the team did a great job, just like setting the tone. Obviously, it was a huge win for the city of Miami, for the organization. There was a lot of celebrities in the house. Some celebrities were next to our bench,” added the 31-year-old. Nov 18, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma (18) drives to the basket against Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo (7) during the second quarter at Kaseya Center. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images “Not to relax, because it’s human nature for you to relax. But win is a win. We’ve been playing good. We scored 140 points. We have OKC coming in a few days. We have two-three days to rest, get ready, and do what we gotta do, and hopefully we can play good basketball against them too.” More Bucks news from Wisconsin Sports Heroics Nov 18, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo (7) reaches for a loose ball against Bucks forward Nate Ament (15) during the fourth quarter at Kaseya Center. item.title: Sophie Cunningham challenges her male haters to 3-point contest
item.description: Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images WNBA star Sophie Cunningham has had enough of armchair critics, and she’s ready to settle things on the court. Sophie Cunningham’s challenge goes straight at one of the tiredest takes in basketball, the idea that any decent guy from the local rec league could hold his own against a WNBA pro. Even with women’s basketball bigger than ever, female players still get hit with the same skepticism about their game every time they log online. The funny thing is, whenever someone actually steps onto the court to test it, reality hits fast. Fans saw Sparks guard Rae Burrell cruise past streamer N3on in a one-on-one, a quick reminder that pro-level talent is on a completely different planet than couch-cushion confidence. Sophie Cunningham challenges men to a three-point contest Speaking on her podcast , Sophie Cunningham finally had enough of guys talking trash about women’s sports from the couch, and decided to call their bluff. She said: “Dude, I think I’ve said enough about where my stance is on this when it comes to boys and girls, I’ll say. But when it comes to regular Joes—what kills me, and even the guys know this—the people talking bad on us women professional athletes, it doesn’t matter the sport, it’s all these men who are laying on the couch, probably eating potato chips. It used to drive me crazy, but now I’m just like, I feel bad for you guys because I don’t know—why are you guys coming after us? “So, what I’m going to say is I think I want to do a challenge here to our listeners, or if you don’t listen, maybe this clip will get out there. I want to find some average Joes—like in the YMCA league and the rec league—who think that they can outshoot me, and have a three-point competition because I’m going to smack that a** every single day of the week. So, I’m challenging all these little people behind the screen who think they can beat me. You won’t.” Honestly, it would be must-see TV. Watching a guy from the local rec league try to keep up with a WNBA player would settle the debate and provide great entertainment, especially considering Cunningham actually shot a higher three-point percentage than Steph Curry this past season. Good luck to whoever volunteers. item.title: Taraba varsity ASUU conditionally suspends strike
item.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Taraba State University (TSU) Branch, has announced the conditional suspension of its ongoing industrial action with immediate effect. In a statement issued on Friday and signed by the Branch Chairman, Dr. Joshua Garba Mbave, the union disclosed that its Congress resolved to suspend the total, comprehensive, and indefinite strike which commenced on October 12, 2026 following an emergency meeting at the ASUU-TSU Secretariat in Jalingo. While confirming the return to academic activities effective November 20, 2026, the union cautioned that sustaining industrial harmony and an uninterrupted academic calendar hinges on mutual trust, accountability, and strict adherence to agreed commitments. ASUU-TSU urged the Taraba State Government, the University Management, and all relevant stakeholders to demonstrate good faith by ensuring the timely and full implementation of all resolutions contained in the joint communiqué and the Memorandum of Action (MoA) to avert a recurrence of the dispute. The union expressed profound appreciation to Governor Agbu Kefas, the Commissioner for Tertiary Education, the Head of Service, and the University Management for their constructive engagement and intervention toward resolving the standoff. It also thanked students, parents, staff, and the wider university community for their patience, solidarity, and understanding throughout the five-week industrial action, appealing for continued cooperation as normal academic activities resume. The post Taraba varsity ASUU conditionally suspends strike appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tyrese Haliburton’s New Indianapolis Bar Gives Caitlin Clark A Special Place on Its Walls
item.description: Aug 6, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark (22) looks on in the first half against the Las Vegas Aces at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images (L); Nov 13, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton sits on the bench in the first half against the New York Knicks at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images (R) Basketball fans in the Indy area continue to get treated to an up-and-coming Tyrese Haliburton-backed sports bar that will now feature a mural of Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark. Clark will be featured as part of the mural inside Haliburton’s new restaurant in Indianapolis, “The Varsity Social Indy.” The announcement from the club on Instagram highlights the Fever star’s inclusion in the restaurant’s artwork, tying together two prominent figures in Indiana basketball. Varsity Social Club, located at 1 Virginia Ave. in downtown Indianapolis, is a new venture from Ambrosia Hospitality Group with Haliburton as a partner and the sole investor. The downtown space Varsity Social Club will occupy has sat vacant since Scotty’s Brewhouse closed in 2018. The new sports-focused dining and entertainment venue spans more than 10,000 square feet and includes lounge and recreational spaces, private rooms, and a patio. The club was originally scheduled to open in Fall 2026, with initial projections targeting September or October 2026. However, at the moment, an exact grand opening date has not been publicly confirmed. However, the team is already active on social media, teasing fans with the behind-the-scenes work that has been going on. One such Instagram Story (now gone) from the club’s official page on November 18, 2026, teased a mural that partially captured Clark’s 22 jersey. A Clark fan shared the news on X (formerly Twitter), with a screenshot of the Instagram Story , which has since gone viral. Varsity Social Club has also shared artworks featuring Haliburton and other sports personalities that fans will see the moment they enter the space. With endorsement from Indiana Pacers star and frequent Ambrosia guest Haliburton, Varsity Social Club will recast the former Scotty’s Brewhouse spot with upgraded technology, a polished new aesthetic, and elevated sports-bar vibes. And one way to tug the heartstrings of Indy people would be to have a mural of one of the most prominent young sports personalities from the area, Clark. item.title: Blues fan snubs Homes Under the Hammer over Villa's Dion Dublin
item.description: Birmingham City supporter George Pollock, pictured with his wife Catherine, turned down the chance of being on the show [George Pollock] A Birmingham City fan has revealed why he refused to appear on Homes Under the Hammer after discovering the presenter was former Aston Villa striker Dion Dublin. George Pollock and his wife Catherine, from Castle Bromwich, were approached by the BBC daytime show's production team after buying a property at auction to renovate and sell on. While Catherine jumped at the chance to feature on the programme, George was rather less enthusiastic, and finding out who would be presenting the episode did not help. George said: "Catherine turned around and told me, 'It's going to be Dion Dublin.' I was like, 'Oh, you do it!' "I didn't really want to spend a day with a Villa player." Dublin played for Aston Villa between 1998 and 2002, scoring 48 goals in 65 appearances, becoming a popular figure at Villa Park. Catherine, meanwhile, was happy to go ahead with the filming, but she knew her husband would not feel the same after learning who would be presenting their episode. "If he says he doesn't want to do something, he's probably not going to. Especially when it comes to football," joked Catherine, who appeared in the episode alone. When the reason for her husband's absence was revealed on the show, Dublin could not help but laugh and commend the fan. "I love that he's a proper Blues fan, good lad," he said. Dion Dublin played for Aston Villa between 1998 and 2002 [BBC/lion production] The couple had bought the property with plans to do it up before selling it but had not initially expected their renovation project to end up on television. The Homes Under the Hammer team regularly keep an eye on property auctions to find potential homes and buyers to feature on the show. For lifelong Blues supporter George, however, there was one problem with the whole arrangement. He explained that his love of Birmingham City was passed down by his father, making the prospect of spending a day with a former Villa player a step too far. He joked: "When you're raised on it, you can't get rid of it and I'm sure the other side would have done the exact same. "I've heard he was a good sport about it," added George, who never did meet Dublin. The story has since sparked plenty of amusement on social media, with football fans enjoying the light-hearted rivalry. George said: "It's petty but it's fun petty." Follow BBC Birmingham on BBC Sounds , Facebook , X and Instagram . item.title: Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United training session filmed by drone and uploaded online amidst security breach
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United training session filmed by drone and uploaded online amidst security breach originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Mauricio Pochettino's very first day on the job at Manchester United has already been met with a crisis as the club was victim of an embarrassing security breach. The Argentine has only just arrived as new United manager, flying into Manchester on Wednesday morning, having departed straight after his final game with the U.S. national team on Tuesday night. He has only a few days to prepare for his debut as Red Devils' boss, a difficult challenge on the road at Anfield. Now, it seems that much of the work he did in his first training session might have to be scrapped as his session was leaked publicly and available to the rest of the world. MORE: All the latest Man United news | Who is on Pochettino's Man United backroom staff? Individual films Man United training session with drone An unknown individual managed to film 12 minutes of Pochettino's first training session at the club's Carrington training ground, which is closed to media and the public. The individual flew a drone high above the training ground and filmed Pochettino running drills and giving tactical instructions to his new Red Devils squad, an event which is usually highly confidential and secretive as to avoid giving opponents clear insight into how teams will line up or approach matches. The video, uploaded to YouTube with the pilot of the drone also narrating the footage, shows various selections of players broken off into position groups training on their own before coming together to take tactical instructions from Pochettino. It appears that the pilot uses a drone with impressive zoom capabilities, and does not seem to cross over the Carrington training ground itself to capture the footage. Early in the video, the narrator states he "does not want to be a nuisance" so he decides to "make full use of the zoom." He later claims "as you can see I'm absolutely miles away," but then pilots the drone along the edge of Carrington's grounds and says "we can get quite a bit closer yet without being a nuisance." The narrator is clearly wary of going too close to the training ground, as about two-thirds through the uploaded video he declares "let's see how much closer I dare go," before flying lower and zooming in on Pochettino leading a huddle with Harry Maguire, Amad Diallo, Ayden Heaven, and others. Man United have refused to comment on the incident, according to the BBC. Drone operator apologises for Man United incident On Friday morning, the person responsible (CC Overview) for the footage removed the clip from YouTube and issued an apology. "I would like to speak about yesterday's incident," they said. "A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone

item.title: 2027: Makinde pledges greater state control of mineral resources
item.description: The Presidential Candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Engr. Seyi Makinde, has pledged to restructure Nigeria’s mining sector by giving state governments and host communities greater control over solid mineral resources within their territories if elected president. Makinde also promised to implement what he described as true fiscal federalism, with resource control as a central component of his administration’s economic restructuring agenda. The proposals are contained in the Makinde-Daura RESET NIGERIA Manifesto, released by the campaign organisation on Friday as part of its RESET NIGERIA Series. Under its vision of a “Federation that Works”, the manifesto faulted the existing arrangement in which major decisions concerning the exploitation of solid minerals are largely taken by the Federal Government, while states and communities affected by mining activities have limited influence. It argued that host communities and state governments bear the consequences of mining operations, including environmental degradation, unsafe storage of hazardous materials, damaged roads, communal conflicts and the burden of responding to emergencies, without adequately benefiting from the resources extracted from their territories. To address the situation, Makinde pledged to initiate a national conversation on restructuring and resource control if elected. The manifesto, however, stated that the proposed exercise would not be another open-ended national conference, but a structured process backed by specific reforms. It disclosed that a Federal Responsibility Review would be completed within the first year of his administration to determine the responsibilities that should remain exclusively with the Federal Government, those requiring national standards but state-level implementation, and functions that should principally be handled by state or local governments. The review would also identify responsibilities requiring published intergovernmental agreements. According to the manifesto, the exercise would produce specific constitutional amendments, legislation, fiscal adjustments and transition arrangements to give effect to the proposed restructuring. On mining regulation, the APM candidate promised to strengthen cooperation between federal and state regulatory authorities, establish publicly accessible registers of mining licences and beneficial ownership, and introduce clearer mechanisms for monitoring compliance and tackling illegal mining. The manifesto clarified that while the Federal Government would continue to issue mining licences under the existing constitutional framework, state governments would be formally involved in the licensing process. It said state governments would have opportunities to review applications and raise concerns relating to land use, environmental protection, community interests and public safety. item.title: Urban Meyer Shoots Down Desmond Howard’s Heisman Thoughts
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) celebrates after scoring a touchdown in the second half of the NCAA football game at Ohio Stadium on Nov. 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. Former Ohio State coach Urban Meyer has publicly rejected 1991 Heisman winner Desmond Howard’s doubts about Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith’s candidacy for the trophy. Howard, speaking on ESPN’s First Take on Nov. 13, questioned whether Smith has delivered in marquee games. “In the last two years, give me one game where Jeremiah Smith … was the difference in a big game,” Howard said. “As much as he puts up these magnificent numbers and these one-handed catches, I need moments against the top competition that make me say ‘he was the guy.'” Meyer, appearing on The Triple Option podcast, was direct in response . “He’s gonna win [the Heisman]. Are we kidding?” he said. Acknowledging that Ohio State’s losses to USC (30-18) and Oregon (41-28) left a “bad taste,” Meyer defended the junior receiver’s effort: “Did he do everything possible to go win those games? Yeah, he did. The fact that Desmond Howard said, ‘I don’t see him making plays in the big games’… I don’t agree with that.” Smith caught 10 passes for 83 yards and a touchdown at USC and seven for 133 yards and a score against Oregon. Meyer added that the award will partly reflect Smith’s body of work, including a national title as a freshman, while insisting the trophy still goes to the best player. Ohio State sits at 7-3 as Smith continues to push his case to become only the sixth wide receiver to win the Heisman.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama has turned his NBA finals humiliation into a revenge tour for the ages
item.description: Victor Wembanyama of the San Antonio Spurs brings the ball upcourt during a game gainst the Utah Jazz at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Sunday. Photograph: Chris Gardner/Getty Images It wouldn’t be exactly right to say Victor Wembanyama didn’t miss a beat after a disastrous NBA finals in June that left him and his San Antonio Spurs defeated, memed and embarrassed. In the Spurs’ first game this season, against an Oklahoma City Thunder team since decimated by injuries, Wemby went an appalling 1-for-13 from the field. Ten of his 12 points came via free throws. After getting blocked by Aday Mara, the Thunder’s 7ft 3in offseason pickup clearly designed to counter the even more towering Wembanyama, he leaned over his knees and muttered furiously to himself as if trying to exorcise an intrusive thought. It brought to mind an image from the NBA finals a few months earlier: Wemby on the floor after being fouled by the Knicks’ Mitchell Robinson, crowing, “I’m in your head!” The Spurs went on to blow a 29-point lead , lose the game and the finals. Now Wemby seemed too preoccupied with the issues within his own dome to worry about wreaking havoc in anybody else’s. Related: Steph Curry’s defense of Ayesha exposes the ugly double standards of sports’ manosphere | Andrew Lawrence Game two saw Wembanyama elect to lay the ball up instead of dunking it in the dying seconds of a close tilt with the Houston Rockets, which the springy Amen Thompson blocked spectacularly . Not a great start, and in a league whose narratives calcify long before sample sizes reach an adequate scale, it allowed for whispers that the Spurs were in trouble. But you could say Wembanyama has not missed a beat since then . After beginning the season 0-2, the Spurs are now 13-3, with 12 of those wins coming in a row before a loss to the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday. San Antonio’s basketball hasn’t been as seamless as those numbers suggest – the starting lineup includes three guards, leaving the offense a bit clunky and wanting for three-point shooting. It also includes Wembanyama, which papers over pretty much every possible problem. Unofficially crowned the best player in the world during last season’s playoffs , Wembanyama has since distanced his closest challengers for that honor. Somebody has stolen Nikola Jokić’s three-point shot and hidden it in a deep hole, signaling what may prove the start of his decline after six consecutive imperious, MVP-caliber seasons, and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander’s efficiency has inevitably suffered as he’s tasked with keeping the injury-ridden Thunder afloat. Wembanyama, meanwhile, has just gotten better, averaging 28.6 points, 11.9 rebounds and countless plays in which his mere presence causes the opposing offense to spontaneously combust through the first 16 games of the season. The Lakers’ Luka Dončić is playing the best basketball of his career this season, averaging gaudy offensive numbers that, if sustained, would represent the most dominant scoring s

item.title: Five Heart Podcast: Beat Ohio State. That’s the Show.
item.description: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 14: Jeremiah Charles #25 of the Nebraska Cornhuskers runs with the ball after his interception against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights in the fourth quarter at SHI Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Piscataway, New Jersey. The Nebraska Cornhuskers defeated the Rutgers Scarlet Knights 31-0. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nebraska football is back in the win column, and the Five Heart Podcast crew is back to figure out what it all means! The Huskers dismantled Rutgers 31-0, recording their first conference shutout since 2003 and their first against a Big Ten opponent. But after four consecutive losses, is this a sign of genuine improvement or simply a struggling opponent making Nebraska look good? The gang breaks down the victory, the ongoing frustrations surrounding Matt Rhule’s program, and whether the Huskers have finally discovered an offensive identity. Next up: Ohio State. With the Buckeyes dealing with quarterback uncertainty and Nebraska coming off its most convincing performance of the season, could the Huskers actually pull off the upset? The crew debates the possibilities, offers score predictions, and asks whether beating Ohio State would change how fans remember this season. There’s also plenty of conversation about Nebraska volleyball, men’s and women’s basketball, recruiting, Kent Pavelka’s farewell season, and former Nebraska athletic director Trev Alberts. Plus, listener questions, the return of Five Heart Theatre, plenty of questionable humor, and the usual detours that make this Husker variety show unlike any other. Grab your favorite beverage and join us!

item.title: Tonda Eckert signs Southampton contract extension after ‘Spygate’ scandal
item.description: Tonda Eckert has signed a contract extension at Southampton after surviving the storm of the ‘Spygate’ scandal . Eckert found himself under immense scrutiny after Southampton were caught spying on their Championship play-off semi-final opponents Middlesbrough last season. An investigation found Saints had also spied on two other teams that seasons and the club were subsequently kicked out of the Championship play-off final and docked four points at the start of the season season, admitting to three breaches of EFL regulations. Eckert accepted responsibility as Southampton opted to stand by their manager despite the controversy, and he was later given a six-week suspended ban - keeping him on the touchline barring any further offences. And despite the hindrance of a points deduction, Southampton have started the season in fine form under Eckert, with the club five points off top spot. The German has now been rewarded with a contract extension that will keep him at the club until 2029. Eckert said: "We've had some conversations that started a couple of weeks ago, and the goal was always clear: to show the same commitment that we have had for the last 12 months. I'm very happy that we have come to the point that we can make it official now. "There is a lot that has happened in the last 12 months, but the commitment from the club, from Dragan, Johannes and Phil, and the supporters, means everything to me. I am very grateful for that. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through - there is a lot more to come." Saints are unbeaten in their last 17 home matches, with Eckert only experiencing one defeat at St Mary’s during his tenure. "I think it's a great commitment from both sides; from the club to Tonda, and from Tonda to the club. I'm very happy that we have achieved this agreement before the end of the international window, allowing us to go into the busy schedule that is ahead of us with clarity,” sporting director Johannes Spors said. "Tonda is very talented and very precise with a great analytical brain, but also has the personality and authority that you need, even at a young age. It is very clear that this is the right place for him, and I'm very happy that he feels that too."

item.title: PPG Paints Arena to host PWHL Takeover Tour game
item.description: PPG Paints Arena in Pittsburgh will host a Professional Women’s Hockey League regular-season game between the Seattle Torrent and the San José Sea Lions on Sunday, Jan. 24, at 2 p.m. PPG Paints Arena in Pittsburgh will host a Professional Women’s Hockey League regular-season game between the Seattle Torrent and the San José Sea Lions on Sunday, Jan. 24, at 2 p.m. The contest is part of the league’s 2026-27 Takeover Tour, which officially begins Jan. 2 and runs through April 10. Pittsburgh’s game is one of 24 stops across North America. The matchup marks the PWHL’s return to Pittsburgh, where PPG Paints Arena previously hosted a neutral-site game during the league’s inaugural season. On March 17, 2024, PWHL Toronto defeated PWHL Montréal 2-1 at the venue. Ticket sales begin soon, with a presale opening this Monday, Nov. 23. General ticket sales will begin Tuesday, Nov. 24, at 10 a.m. Eastern Time. The January game will feature forward Laila Edwards, an alumna of the local Pens Elite youth hockey program. Edwards was selected fourth overall by San José in the 2026 PWHL Draft, becoming the first draft pick in the expansion franchise’s history. Marcel Braithwaite, president of business operations for the Pittsburgh Penguins, welcomed the return of professional women’s hockey to the city. “The Penguins organization is thrilled to welcome the PWHL back to Pittsburgh for its Takeover Tour in January,” Braithwaite said. “The growth of women’s hockey nationally has had a profound impact on youth hockey here in our community, and this is a great opportunity for Pittsburgh fans to welcome some of the world’s best players to our city.” The 2026-27 Takeover Tour represents the largest neutral-site tour in league history, scheduling 24 games across 19 cities in the United States and Canada. Spanning 99 days from Jan. 2 through April 10, the tour will feature all 12 league teams, with each team competing in four neutral-site games. The itinerary includes visits to nine new markets and returns to 10 cities that have previously hosted tour games.Amy Scheer, the PWHL executive vice president of business operations, highlighted the tour’s role in expanding access to professional women’s hockey across North America. “The Takeover Tour gives us the opportunity to bring the energy and excitement of PWHL games to fans beyond our home markets,” Scheer said. “With 24 games across 19 cities this season, we’re creating more opportunities for fans to see our players compete, returning to communities that have supported the league while introducing the PWHL to new audiences and strengthening our presence across North America. Through meaningful community engagement surrounding the games, we’re inspiring the next generation of players and making hockey more accessible to communities and fans who may not otherwise have the opportunity to experience it.” The Takeover Tour has expanded steadily since its inception. Over its first two seasons, the tour drew 323,232 fans across 25

item.title: Dodgers notes: Tarik Skubal, Kiké Hernández, Hyeseong Kim
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 03: Tarik Skubal #29 of the Los Angeles Dodgers pitches during the sixth inning against the Atlanta Braves in game one of the National League Division Series at Dodger Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The impending lockout is less than two weeks away, and after a relatively dormant start to the offseason, the stove is starting to heat up. Several key moves this week include Sonny Gray returning to the Minnesota Twins, reigning NLCS MVP Jake Bauers officially shipping up to Boston, and the Colorado Rockies swinging a move for right-handers Davis Martin and Luis Castillo from the Chicago White Sox. The biggest prize of the offseason— Tarik Skubal— has met with four teams this week; the Dodgers, the Toronto Blue Jays, the New York Mets and the San Diego Padres. Even with a potential salary cap in place after the fallout of the lockout, several teams are willing to “break the bank” if they get their hands on Skubal, reports Jeff Passan of ESPN . By the time he signs — and it could be sooner than later — it will be the largest deal for a pitcher in baseball history. For a player such as Skubal, even the teams that want a salary cap are willing to break the bank. Throughout his time with the Dodgers, Kiké Hernández has become a fan favorite for his quirky personality and for his big moments in the postseason. Since Hernández was reacquired by the Dodgers in the summer of 2023, his presence was crucial in helping the team win two consecutive championships. But, could his time as a Dodger be up? Jake Storiale and former big-league infielder Trevor Plouffe discuss the future of Hernández’s time in Los Angeles with Doug McKain of Dodgers Nation in the latest episode of the Talkin’ Baseball podcast . With just one year left on his current contract, utility man Hyeseong Kim hasn’t proven himself to be an everyday player at the big league level with the Dodgers. Jack Harris of the California Post notes on Kim’s uncertain position with the Dodgers, noting that the team is still hopeful that his bat can fully emerge. “Hopefully,” general manager Brandon Gomes said last week, “he’ll take a step forward on the swing mechanics and [we can] get him into a really good place offensively.”

item.title: Wild GM Responds to Dylan Larkin Trade Package Rumors
item.description: The Dylan Larkin trade saga has produced plenty of rumors, but Minnesota Wild general manager Bill Guerin wants to make one thing clear: Nobody outside the two organizations knows exactly what Minnesota has offered the Detroit Red Wings. With reports circulating about a massive package involving several players and multiple first-round draft picks, Guerin recently pushed back on the speculation. His comments raise an interesting question about how much of the reported trade package is actually accurate.’ Mar 21, 2026; Saint Paul, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Wild general manager Bill Guerin presents defensemen Jared Spurgeon (46) with a silver stick in honor of his 1000 career NHL games before a tilt against the Dallas Stars at Grand Casino Arena. Mandatory Credit: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Bill Guerin Addresses Dylan Larkin Trade Rumors During a November 12 appearance on Minneapolis radio, Guerin was asked about reports that Minnesota had included young forward Danila Yurov in a potential deal for Larkin. Rather than confirming or denying the rumored offer, the Wild GM made it clear that the public doesn’t know what has been discussed. “Look, I know there are reports out there that we have offered him up, but nobody knows what I’ve offered, except Detroit,” Guerin said, according to NHL.com . Guerin’s response is significant because several reports have detailed potential Minnesota trade packages as the Wild continue pursuing Larkin. As Heavy reported , the Minnesota GM’s comments cast doubt on the accuracy of the rumored offers without eliminating the possibility that Yurov has been discussed. What Have the Wild Reportedly Offered Detroit? One of the most substantial reported packages included Yurov, former Michigan State standout Charlie Stramel, veteran forward Ryan Hartman, and two first-round draft picks. The Red Wings reportedly turned down that offer , although the exact details have not been publicly confirmed by either organization. Other reports have suggested different combinations of prospects and draft selections, including a potential package centered around Yurov and three first-round picks. That creates considerable uncertainty about what Minnesota has actually put on the table and whether Detroit has received an offer it would seriously consider accepting. For the Red Wings, the situation remains complicated because Larkin’s value goes beyond his offensive production. Detroit would need a significant return for its longtime center, particularly with interim general manager Shawn Horcoff attempting to improve the organization’s long-term outlook. Does Guerin’s Response Change Anything? The most important distinction is that Guerin did not publicly deny making an offer for Larkin. He also didn’t explicitly rule out including Yurov, meaning his comments should not be interpreted as proof that the reported trade packages are entirely false. Meanwhile, Detroit has continued holding firm

item.title: Travis Kelce Gets Caitlin Clark To Reveal Her Notre Dame Loyalty On New Heights
item.description: Caitlin Clark Caitlin Clark has a hard time slipping through any building unnoticed. So a hat and a pair of sunglasses had to do the heavy lifting at Notre Dame Stadium. The Indiana Fever star revealed this week on the ‘New Heights’ podcast that she attended Notre Dame’s win over then-No. 1 Miami on Nov. 7 in a low-key disguise. She also admitted that she grew up a Fighting Irish fan and nearly picked the program for college. Travis Kelce wanted to know why an Iowa icon was watching Notre Dame. Clark explained that it has become a yearly habit. “ I try to make it to, like, one Notre Dame game a year. I grew up a Notre Dame fan. I wanted to go to Notre Dame ,” Clark said. “I try to make it to one Notre Dame game a year. I grew up a Notre Dame fan.” — Caitlin Clark on attending Notre Dame’s win over No. 1 Miami — Drew Mentock (@AndrewMentock) November 19, 2026 The setup was part of the fun. Clark did not ask for a field pass. She took ordinary seats, and her description is hard to beat. “ I had on like a hat and sunglasses, and I was actually in the second to last row of like the normal bowl, like normal seats ,” Clark said. “ Yeah, nobody knew, I mean some people knew. ” For Clark, the draw was the atmosphere, including a tailgate beforehand with actor Jason Sudeikis, who was the guest picker on College GameDay that week. She picked a good night for it. Notre Dame beat Miami 31-24 in a game that ended with a controversial late call. The win knocked the Hurricanes off the top spot, and quarterback CJ Carr threw for 319 yards and 3 touchdowns. The Irish are now 9-1. Marcus Freeman’s team is poised to return to the College Football Playoff, so Clark picked a season-defining night to show up. Notre Dame faces SMU next, and the Irish will try to keep that momentum going. Why Caitlin Clark Still Has Notre Dame In Her Heart The loyalty goes back to her recruiting days in 2019. Clark narrowed her list to Iowa, Iowa State, and Notre Dame. Her family leaned toward South Bend, and she has never hidden that. “ They recruited me. It was between Notre Dame and Iowa, and then I picked Iowa ,” Clark said. “ But Notre Dame is just so cool, the history of everything. ” She has been even more direct before. “ My family wanted me to go to Notre Dame ,” Clark has said. “ But it’s NOTRE DAME! ‘Rudy’ was one of my favorite movies. How could you not pick Notre Dame? ” There is one limit to her loyalty, and Hawkeyes fans will like it. Clark would not cheer for the Irish if they ever faced Iowa. The two schools met 24 times between 1921 and 1968, but the series went quiet decades ago. A conversation with then-Iowa assistant coach Jan Jensen helped tip her final call toward the Hawkeyes. She went on to become the face of Iowa basketball, but her Notre Dame fandom never went away. Her fall has been busy outside the WNBA season. She popped up at Penn’s game at Illinois on Nov. 5 to support Fran McCaffery, the father of her boyfriend, Connor McCaffery. Illinois freshman Quenti

item.title: Browns rookie KC Concepcion on his speech impediment: ‘I fight a constant battle’
item.description: The best part about the Cleveland Browns being flexed to Sunday Night Football for Week 12 versus the Las Vegas Raiders is what it says about the team’s quality of play and record . The second best part is how it allows the City of Cleveland and Browns fans to get the spotlight for just how great both are. Then we get to the third, and maybe even deeper pieces of positivity: A national audience getting to know a Browns roster full of what seems like fun, positive young players. While the list is long, rookie WR KC Concepcion sits at the top of players Cleveland fans have had no choice but to embrace for their personality, hard work, and performance. For Concepcion, it starts with his “constant battle” with a speech impediment . Not only is Concepcion dealing with his stutter, but the young receiver actively seeks out opportunities to speak in public, despite his struggle. Concepcion ensures that he speaks to the Browns media as often as he can, despite not being required to do so, and also spoke with Jordan Schultz on the national level during the bye week. Once again having a chance to inspire others, Concepcion talked about how his battle with speech encourages him in other areas of his life: A kid on my son’s hockey team has a speech impediment. I told him I would be interviewing KC Concepcion on my show, and he wanted me to ask him this question. Everything KC said here is inspiring for young and old. ❤️🙏 https://t.co/ldgxULV28K pic.twitter.com/cFNd2FrZ60 — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 20, 2026 You can see the whole interview with Concepcion below, where he talks about a number of topics with Schultz: On your list of favorite current Browns, how high is Concepcion? item.title: Merab Dvalishvili has his next opponent in mind, and it’s not Umar Nurmagomedov
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 18: Merab Dvalishvili of Georgia and Umar Nurmagomedov of Russia strike each other in a bantamweight title fight during UFC 311 at Intuit Dome on January 18, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Merab Dvalishvili is eager to get back into the cage following his second loss to Petr Yan, and he knows exactly who he wants to fight next. Dvalishvili had a big 2025 which saw him attempt to defend the UFC bantamweight title four times in one year. He was successful three times, beating Umar Nurmagomedov, Sean O’Malley, and Corey Sandhagen. A fourth title defense didn’t go as well: Petr Yan dismantled “The Machine” and took Merab’s belt. Dvalishvili spent 2026 wrestling for Real American Freestyle and waiting for an immediate rematch against Yan. That finally took place at UFC 333 in October, and Yan once again defeated Dvalishvili. Now on the outside of the title contender’s circle looking in, Merab shared what he’d like to do next with Nina Drama. 🚨👀 Merab Dvalishvili reveals he will ‘most likely’ fight Song Yadong next, while Sean O’Malley is expected to rematch Petr Yan for the bantamweight title. (via @Ninadrama ) pic.twitter.com/lpzPZVHXh4 — Home of Fight (@Home_of_Fight) November 19, 2026 “I think I should fight Song Yadong because they’re not going to give a title fight,” Dvalishvili said. “I think Sean O’Malley is going to fight for the belt. I should fight Song Yadong. I will fight whenever.” It’s still unclear what the UFC plans to do with the bantamweight division. Both Sean O’Malley and Song Yadong have decent claims on the next title shot. We’d give the edge to O’Malley, but it probably comes down to whether the promotion has a big event in China coming up that Yan is healthy for. If Yadong doesn’t get Yan next, will the UFC really set their popular Chinese striker up against Dvalishvili? Yan just got past Umar Nurmagomedov in August, proving he can deal with top shelf wrestling. Would they make him prove it again? Or will they look at recent events involving Dvalishvili and Nurmagomedov and say that is a rematch that has to happen sooner rather than later?

item.title: “One Debate America Could Not Survive” – OutKick Reporter Dreads Potential Sophie Cunningham-Sydney Sweeney “Bond Girl” Face Off After Clay Travis Looks Past Fever Guard
item.description: Sophie Cunningham - Image © Imagn Images Conservative media outlet OutKick’s Bobby Burack believes America won’t “survive” a Sophie Cunningham vs. Sydney Sweeney debate. Burack commented after OutKick founder Clay Travis said Sweeney is the better candidate to play “Bond Girl” over Cunningham. The Fever guard expressed her wish to become a “Bond Girl” on Thursday on X. “okay but for real… I want to be the next Bond girl. Someone help!” she said. Cunningham’s post drew mixed reactions. Travis has often hailed her as a marketable athlete, but doesn’t think she should be considered for a “Bond Girl” role. Meanwhile, Burack dreads a debate between Sweeney and Cunningham. “Sydney Sweeney vs. Sophie Cunningham is one debate America could not survive. It would tear us apart beyond repair,” Burack said. Travis said Sweeney is the “obvious” choice because she’s more popular and several brands have endorsed her. Travis also feels acting is harder than people think and Cunningham won’t be a natural fit. He cited Ray Allen’s performance in “He Got Game” alongside Denzel Washington to justify his remark. Travis said Allen didn’t do a great job and was overshadowed after being cast alongside a legend like Washington. Sophie Cunningham expresses wish to become WNBA commissioner Sophie Cunningham, 30, still has several years left as a player. She remains one of the league’s most solid role players, able to defend and knock down shots at a high clip. However, Cunningham is already thinking about her career after basketball. She’s aspiring to become the WNBA commissioner. In an interview with Maxim on Wednesday, Cunningham said: “I do think being the WNBA commissioner would be awesome. Sometimes you just need someone to lead with love and experience, who has played in the league, and understands what the players need—but also understands the business side of things. And I think that I am developing that type of mindset. We’ll see what happens. I think it’d be fun. It’s not out of the question.” Cunningham is already one of the most marketable players. Since joining the Indiana Fever in 2025, her endorsements have gone up. Cunningham has proved she has the acumen to run a business, which has instilled confidence in her aspirations to become league commissioner. According to ESPN , the WNBA is searching for its next commissioner and has interviewed a dozen candidates. NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum will become WNBA commissioner if the league doesn’t hire a candidate before 2027. item.title: Cadillac Will Stay a Ferrari Customer Through 2029 and Wait for F1’s V8 Engines
item.description: Cadillac will stay a Ferrari customer through 2029 and debut its own power unit in 2030, when F1 plans to switch to V8s, CEO Dan Towriss said on Nov. 19. Cadillac has backed the FIA’s push for a switch to V8 power units from the 2030 F1 season. Earlier this week, the governing body posted graphics saying a new V8 framework had been agreed in principle, then deleted them, leaving the move still unconfirmed. F1 team bosses at the Las Vegas Grand Prix confirmed that there is an agreement in principle, but the FIA has yet to make it official. It wants to put the 2030 rules to the World Motor Sport Council on Dec. 10. Cadillac, the newest team on the grid, has welcomed the move as it gets ready to open its new power unit facility in December. Cadillac Backs FIA for V8 Move “Yeah, I think we’re glad to really see the series coming together under the leadership of the FIA to set that direction for a V8 in 2030, so we’re super happy with that,” Towriss, CEO of Cadillac F1 and TWG Motorsports, said in the FIA press conference in Las Vegas. “Our new power unit facility opens up on December 18th, so as a new manufacturer coming into the sport, the direction is obviously very helpful. We’re excited about the direction, and the crew’s hard at work getting ready.” Asked which engine the new facility in Charlotte, North Carolina, would work on first, Towriss said the team already had a V6 base ready and had started working on V8 designs as well, laying down the foundation to build on. Dan Towriss, CEO of Cadillac F1 and TWG Motorsports, in the FIA press conference at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Nov. 19, 2026. Image Credit: Cadillac F1 Team General Motors Has Worked on Both V6 and V8 Designs “Well, for a period of time, we were working on both,” said Towriss. “So, they’ve already got a V6 base to build off of, and working towards the V8. There are a number of designs that are in motion now, and yeah, so there’s a lot of good foundation for what we’re trying to build and the direction we’re headed in.” Cadillac joined F1 in 2026 as a Ferrari customer team, with General Motors due to supply its own power unit from the 2029 season. Cadillac Will Stay a Ferrari Customer in 2029 Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac MAC-26 and Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari SF-26 at the Dutch Grand Prix, Aug. 21, 2026. Image Credit: Cadillac F1 Team Asked whether it still made sense to build its own engine for 2029, when it would race for only one season before the V8s arrive, Towriss said Cadillac would remain a Ferrari customer through 2029 and start afresh in 2030 as a works team, with General Motors supplying the power unit. “Yeah, we would remain a customer of Ferrari through ’29 and bring the Cadillac power unit online in 2030 with the V8,” he said.

item.title: Real Madrid academy talent faces key decision as Spain and Argentina fight for services
item.description: Real Madrid academy talent faces key decision as Spain and Argentina fight for services Real Madrid’s academy is filled with young stars who hope to make it big in Madrid, defending the club’s crest and going down as a legend in the history books. The current generation of young stars, in that sense, is a little extra-special as they performed brilliantly with the Juvenil A side last season. Under Alvaro Lopez’s command, the youth side won not only the league title and the Champions Cup and the UEFA Youth League, thereby closing a treble in their division. One of the players who was a key pillar in the side, and even the captain, was Carlos Diez. The nationality conundrum As revealed by AS in a recent report, two top nations are currently battling to earn Diez’s loyalty in the long run, and the battle is more fascinating than one would expect. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Fabrica Madrid (@fabrica.madrid) Born in Madrid, the player is eligible to play for the Spanish national team who are interested in keeping him on their cards. Concurrently, his mother holds an Argentine citizenship and he thus has an added option of playing for the Albacete. Given the form the player has been in for Real Madrid C, and his overall form last season, it is not surprising to see a tussle for his services. The final decision, needless to say, will rest with Diez himself. A battle to lure the star As further relayed by the outlet, both the Spanish and Argentine federations have made moves to show the player their interest and win his attention, all of which has happened in the recent past. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Cantera Real Madrid C.F. (@realmadridacademy) Diez is on Paco Gallardo’s list to join the Spanish under-20 setup and can earn a call-up for the under-20 FIFA World Cup next year. He was previously a member of the under-19 selection for Spain but has not been called up again after January. Diego Placente, the manager of Argentina’s under-20 team, was keen to call up the player during the recent international break to give him a taste of Argentine football and lure him. Real Madrid were even informed of the invitation, but the club decided against sending the player as given that only friendlies were scheduled. Nevertheless, Argentina’s U20 side will play the South American U20 championships early next year, and it remains to be seen if Diez earns the call-up.

item.title: England will need fire and pride to beat New Zealand – Steve Borthwick
item.description: Steve Borthwick has called on England to ignite against New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday by showing the emotion needed to inflict another upset on the All Blacks . England have rebuilt following their worst Six Nations on record by winning four successive Tests, including this month’s victories over Australia and Japan that have kept them in the hunt for a place in the Nations Championship final . New Zealand will provide a valuable gauge of their progress but are reeling from being upstaged 35-28 by Wales in Cardiff last Saturday in one of the sport’s great upsets. Former England boss Eddie Jones stated that the All Blacks’ backlash will be “violent” and following a 13-try rout of Japan, Borthwick has reverted to his strongest possible matchday 23 to meet the challenge. Tactically Will Joseph coming in for ankle injury victim Immanuel Feyi-Waboso on the left wing is the only change to the starting XV and bench that dismantled Australia in the autumn opener. “We are all well aware of that history with New Zealand,” Borthwick said. “Emotion is a key part of the game. While ensuring the team is tactically well set and physically ready to go, it’s also about ensuring they are mentally ready to go. “I said before the autumn that I wanted players to bring the fire and pride they have shown when they’re wearing their club shirts to an England shirt. “We want to work really hard for each other and that’s not just technique, it’s not just tactics, that has also got to be a load of emotion. “The players need to bring that pride and that willingness to go that bit further for each other. “To play against New Zealand, you have to go that bit further. The players understand that. “Every experience adds up as you build towards the World Cup, I’m always aware of that, but at this point in the week, in the middle of the series, all that matters is Saturday afternoon.” Exceptional Joseph won his duel with Cadan Murley to replace Feyi-Waboso on the strength of his five-try haul against Japan that saw the 24-year-old Test rookie equal the national record for individual tries scored in a match. Feyi-Waboso lit up England’s attack against Australia until he limped off at half-time and Joseph, another explosive runner, has been instructed to perform a similar roaming role against New Zealand. “Will’s point of difference is his ball carrying and we saw his ability to beat defenders against Japan,” Borthwick said. “He’s been exceptional in that regard. “I want to see him look for the ball, within our structures. Go find the ball in the middle. Be an option at first receiver as well.” Flanker Ollie Chessum, centre Seb Atkinson and full-back George Furbank are back after recovering from the respective shoulder, hip and groin problems that forced them to miss the demolition of Japan. item.title: Raheem Mostert tells Kansas City Chiefs what to do with Kenneth Walker in Week 11
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Raheem Mostert does not want to see Kenneth Walker III in action this weekend when the Kansas City Chiefs take on the Arizona Cardinals. Walker impressed in Week 9 against the New York Jets, managing 102 rushing yards and one touchdown. But he was then listed on the Chiefs’ injury report ahead of the previous game week and missed out on the 35-15 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Now, when speaking via CBS, Mostert has urged caution over bringing Walker back too early, saying the ‘smartest move’ is for him to miss the game. He said: “You gotta rest him. Like you mentioned, he was a frontrunner for the league MVP and Offensive Player of the Year, whatever. But I would rest him, I mean groins are no joke as well. These soft-tissue injuries. They linger on and on and if you don’t take care of them, you know. “Yeah, you have to be 100 percent but these injuries, it has to be like 120 percent. You got to make sure you really feel good, don’t feel any type of inkling pain because it can prolong your injury and you’ll be out even more. “So, yeah, they’re playing against the Cardinals. Right now, having him just on the wayside and not play this game is the smartest move.” Kansas City Chiefs injury report before Arizona Cardinals At present, the Chiefs’ injury report includes Walker and says that he did not participate in practice on Wednesday or Thursday. Jaylon Moore and Trey Smith are the other two players who are listed as not practising this week alongside the former Seattle Seahawks man. Elsewhere, Jon Gaines II is the only player from the Cardinals who reportedly did not practice on Thursday. At present, the Cardinals are 3-7 this season and with much tougher games coming up, leaving Walker out on Sunday does make sense for the Chiefs. They will play the 8-1 Buffalo Bills in Week 12, followed by games against the 6-4 Los Angeles Rams and the 7-2 Cincinnati Bengals. Read more: Stephen A. item.title: Jason Whitlock exposes Deion Sanders’ ‘one of the oldest tricks in the book’ to not get fired
item.description: Photo by Matthew Jonas/MediaNews Group/Boulder Daily Camera via Getty Images Sports analyst Jason Whitlock shows no love for Colorado Buffaloes head coach Deion Sanders. The Colorado Buffaloes are off to an underwhelming 2-5 start to the season, and they are currently the second-worst team in the Big 12 conference. Amid the Buffaloes’ poor form, many are wondering if it’s time for the program to move on from Deion Sanders. For now, fans have sympathized with Coach Prime as he’s also dealing with some major security threats due to the program’s slump. However, sports analyst Jason Whitlock thinks this is all an act. Jason Whitlock thinks Deion Sanders is using threats to avoid losing his job Whitlock is known for his rather ruthless takes on sports personalities, and he didn’t spare Coach Prime by going on a lengthy rant about the NFL legend. “Deion is fighting tooth and nail not to get fired. This is one of the oldest tricks in the book. Ronny Thompson planted racist letters in his office at Ball State,” Whitlock wrote on X . “Deion wants you to believe no one threatens Lane Kiffin or other coaches. Deion is playing the race card. Predictable,” he added. Considering how passionate fans are about college football, they often cross boundaries during slumps. But Whitlock’s just made a massive allegation about Sanders. This could go sideways rather quickly for Whitlock, as bringing Coach Prime’s race into the conversation seems unnecessary and could infuriate his loyal supporters. item.title: Staff score predictions for Clemson’s tough ACC road matchup against Duke
item.description: Clemson football will look to get back in the win column Saturday night when the Tigers travel to Durham for their final ACC matchup of the 2026 regular season against No. 24 Duke . With just two games remaining, Clemson (6-4, 4-3 ACC) finds itself in a position few expected entering the year. Dabo Swinney’s team has endured another disappointing season, and last weekend’s 20-6 loss to Georgia Tech only added to the frustration surrounding the program. The Tigers now face an even bigger challenge with major questions at quarterback. Starter Tait Reynolds suffered a season-ending knee injury against the Yellow Jackets, while Christopher Vizzina was also knocked out of the contest with a concussion. Former walk-on Trent Pearman is now expected to make his first career start. Pearman has attempted just 19 passes this season, completing 10 for 86 yards with two interceptions. His lack of experience could make things difficult for an offense that has already struggled to find any consistency. Duke (7-3, 4-3 ACC) has enjoyed a much better season and enters Saturday’s matchup ranked No. 24 in the Coaches Poll. The Blue Devils are coming off a 36-25 loss to Miami, but they gave the Hurricanes a competitive game behind a strong performance from Nate Sheppard, who totaled 224 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns. Recent meetings between these programs have also gone Duke’s way. Clemson has lost two straight against the Blue Devils, including a stunning 46-45 defeat at Memorial Stadium last November. The Tigers still lead the all-time series 37-18-1. Saturday’s contest is set for 7:30 p.m. ET at Wallace Wade Stadium and will be televised nationally on ESPN. With Clemson dealing with significant injuries and Duke looking to add another victory to an already successful season, the Tigers have their work cut out for them. Here’s how our staff predicts Saturday night’s matchup between Clemson and Duke will unfold. Alex Turri: Duke 30, Clemson 10 What a weird feeling this is. Predicting a Clemson loss is one thing, but a blowout loss is another. Regardless, that’s where we are with this team. Clemson’s new starting quarterback Trent Pearman is getting thrown into a matchup with not only one of the hottest teams in the ACC, but the country. I don’t really see how the Tigers score today, and the defense will suffer because of it. Steve Holley: Duke 23, Clemson 7 I haven't been predicted Clemson to lose by this big a score since Dabo Swinney led the program to the highest of highs. In case you haven't noticed, he's also guided the program to some pretty bad lows this season. Bottom line: no team wins with a third-string quarterback (at best?) starting his first game in Week 12 of the season. Duke has played solid football all season, giving Manny Diaz his best team. Contact us at @Clemson_Wire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook for ongoing coverage of Clemson Tigers news, notes and opinions .
